mu_name_from: MuPlayer.PartsForClass in the old client: the body a class wears with no armour equipped is HelmClass{NN}, ArmorClass{NN} and so on, and the numbering runs one over MU's zero-based classes - so Class01 is the Dark Wizard.
part_note: The torso, 284 triangles. Bound to 62 on Bip01 Spine, 48 on Bip01 Spine1, 29 on Bip01 L UpperArm, 29 on Bip01 R UpperArm, 7 on Bip01 R Clavicle, 6 on Bip01 L Forearm, 6 on Bip01 R Forearm, 3 on Bip01 L Clavicle.
sheet_from: Data/Player/HQSkinClass101.OZJ (256x256), from the Season 17 client (third_party/MuClient_S17_v1.19.74). All five of the Dark Wizard's parts name it.
unstack_why:
Refuses the UV un-stacking, and it is the only asset in the tree that does. With it on, the buckled vest disappears from the bake: 102 of this part's 150 triangles have UV centres on that vest and the island list agrees, yet the atlas held nothing but a bare arm and featureless grey. Off, the vest comes back with its buckles and straps and the part matches the Dark Knight's, which never triggers the step at all - his torso arrives 0% stacked where this one arrives 5.9%, and 69 of its 150 faces get moved off their twin.

Found only after the Figma sheet, the texel density, the UV convention and transfer_albedo had each been cleared by measurement. It is a workaround rather than a fix: the step writes to BAKE_UV and leaves ORIGINAL_UV alone, which is the right shape, so why the moved faces then sample the wrong region of the sheet is still unexplained.
model_from: Season 17's remake of MU's Dark Wizard body, read out of Data/Player/ArmorClass01.bmd in the S17 client: a version-14 file, which MuExtract opens through Webzen's ModulusCryptor (pipeline/MuExtract/MuAssets/Crypto). It replaced MuMain's ArmorClass01 on 2026-10-15 at the user's call ("okey lets make new dw and sm then", after seeing the two side by side). Its 51 bones are the first 51 of player.bmd's, by name and order, so it rides our rig and clips as MuMain's did.

uv_overrides.why: The bare upper arm, the sheet's bottom-left block.

uv_overrides_why: One shell carries the vest and the bare arms, as MuMain's did. Sampled under every face's UV centre: the rectangle takes all 118 faces that read as skin and 2 at its edge; nothing outside it reads as skin.
material_note: cloth for the navy vest and its silver wing embroidery; skin for the bare arms, lifted out by uv_overrides.
